keyFindings.description: Since 90d28d94 the disk-growth steps restart every hub pod when maxFileStoreGb follows diskSizeGb by default (no streamMaxBytes, no explicit maxFileStoreGb). The max-file-store annotation changes with diskSizeGb, so the StatefulSet created in step 5 has a new template revision, and its controller rolls the three orphaned pods. Step 5 (and the intro at :327-328) still says no pod is replaced and that 'the reloader applies' the new limit. The pod-template list at :322-323 also omits the store limit. Say what happens, or how to keep the pods (pin maxFileStoreGb to its current value during the growth).

The depends-on rationale at :248-253 and docs/nats-hub.md:783-787 still names only the session user and auth.conf. The max-file-store roll needs the same order (a pod restarted on the old nats.conf would hold the higher limit, and the later reload of the lower one is refused and blocks every reload after it). State the rule for both annotations, so no one makes the annotation conditional on the session user.

The earlier-build text (README:304-308, nats-hub.md:840-844) leaves out that today's listener answers /healthz 200 'starting' from process start until its durable binds (cmd/listener/main.go:340-358). So the advertiser advertises the second host and marks it ready for most of each 135 s wait, the rollout and budget count it as serving, and the host then leaves the Service when its listener exits. Also, CHANGELOG.md:18-25 does not name the INFRA-557 prerequisite.
